newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ATHERTON SHOWS GLIMPES OF REGAINING FORM.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ATHERTON SHOWS GLIMPES OF REGAINING FORM.

text.p: England captain Mike Atherton showed glimpses of returning to form for Lancashire in the English county championship on Thursday, barely a week before the opening one-day international against Australia.
The England opener, who had scored just 96 runs in eight innings, hit 48 not out as Lancashire staged a second innings fightback against Nottinghamshire at Old Trafford.
Lancashire finished at 133 for one, five runs behind, with John Crawley on 64 not out, following his unbeaten 51 in the first innings.
England meet the tourists in the first of three one-dayers at Headingley next Thursday.
Graham Rose hammered 191 and Richard Harden 103 to set a seventh wicket record stand of 279 for Somerset against Sussex at Taunton.
Somerset were in deep trouble at 67 for six in reply to the visitors' 241 before Rose and Harden carried the side to 409 all out. Sussex were six for no wicket in their second innings at the close.
Number nine David Millns struck his second career century to help Leicestershire recover from a poor start against Hampshire at Southampton.
Millns arrived with the champions in trouble at 157 for seven in reply to Hampshire's first innings total of 285.
At the close, Millns was 101 not out and Leicestershire were 326 for nine.
England and Glamorgan spinner Robert Croft finished with five for 33 as Kent slipped to 154 all out at Canterbury.
Starting the day at 67 for two, Kent lost their last eight wickets for 87, giving Glamorgan a lead of 125 before rain stopped play at lunch.
Warwickshire need another 172 runs with seven wickets in hand to beat Yorkshire on a tricky pitch at Edgbaston.
Warwickshire face an in-form Darren Gough who picked up two second innings wickets, to follow his four-wicket haul in the first innings, to leave Warwickshire at 76 for three.
Early leaders Gloucestershire grabbed a first innings lead of 256 over Surrey at The Oval, and then had Surrey in trouble at 59 for three in their second innings.
Australian Dean Jones hit 53 as Derbyshire made 178 to take a 32-run first innings lead against Middlesex at Lord's. Middlesex were 108 for three at the close.
Durham moved to within one run of a first innings lead at Chelmsford, progressing to 236 for five in reply to Essex's 237.
